title: Escher Menagerie
description: Interlocking-creature tessellations in the manner of M.C. Escher — birds, fish and reptiles that tile the plane with no gaps. A base lattice is bent edge-by-edge into a creature silhouette using the conserved-bump trick (the bite taken from one tile becomes the bulge of the next), so every tile is the same shape and they lock together perfectly. Each is then given an eye and a few wing, fin or limb strokes and coloured by its orientation: a flock of two-tone birds, a school of fish swimming in alternating rows, or a lattice of three-colour lizards rotating 120 degrees about every vertex, the way Escher's Reptiles do. Creature size, shape depth, markings, outline and palette are live across seven palettes plus Random; it renders once and holds, re-deals on a new seed, and the whole field can be rotated.
